commitResults.messageTitle: Improve command guidance and member readability
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace linked help with a bundled eight-command guide and show member
fields in wrapping rows. Apply a consistent beige palette to the main
window, guide, validation states, and alerts for easier reading.

Preserve saved data on failed writes, restore a failed clear, and prevent
accidental retries of already-applied changes. Handle malformed storage,
long email input, whitespace-separated fields, and invalid window bounds.

Keep the user and developer guides aligned with the working increment,
while retaining the complete planned MVP requirements separately.

commitResults.messageTitle: Return focus to the main window after help
commitResults.messageBody:
Give the command guide an owner and explicitly restore main-window
focus when it closes. This keeps Escape and Close guide from leaving
keyboard users without a focused command input on macOS.

Verify both close paths in the native preview and rerun the full
286-test suite, Checkstyle, and JAR build on Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement Ian's list and clear requirements
commitResults.messageBody:
Match the specified empty, singular, plural, usage, and failure messages.
Keep list read-only and restore the complete roster in its stored order.
Make clear count hidden members, save even an empty roster, reset the
view after success, and restore records and filters when saving fails.

Use atomic file replacement to satisfy clear's saved-data guarantee.
Keep member cards readable with labelled wrapping rows and beige colours.
Document and test the two commands while leaving the other owners'
command implementations at the starter behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Verify member-card content and wrapping in JavaFX
commitResults.messageBody:
Exercise real off-screen layout at a narrow width so labels, sorted tags,
empty tag rows, and long values cannot regress unnoticed. Use a virtual
display on Linux CI to run these checks without opening app windows.

All 258 tests, Checkstyle, coverage generation, and JAR packaging pass
locally on Java 25 with the host-matching JavaFX runtime.
